subject: Control-plane partitioning and cross-tenant leakproofing — architecture snapshot and deliverables
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@nimbusai.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@secure-audits.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Control-plane partitioning and cross-tenant leakproofing — architecture snapshot and deliverables

Hi Alex / Olivia —

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. As NimbusAI prepares for the SOC 2 readiness window, your audit team asked for a concise security architecture packet that explains how Redwood handles control-plane isolation and prevents cross-tenant leakage for Dedicated and Private deployments. Our goal is to give you a single narrative + artefact bundle that covers both high-level boundaries and the specific evidence items auditors typically request.

To get the packet started, please find the initial ask below and the two attached diagrams (stubs):
- Requested scope: Dedicated and Private (VPC + on-prem) deployments, specifically control-plane partitioning, API authentication/authorization boundaries, KV cache isolation, and egress assurance.
- Deliverables we plan to provide: network topology diagram (control + data plane lanes), sequence flow for first-party control-plane calls, tenant-guard rails summary, KMS boundary table, and manifest of evidence for SIG/CAIQ/SOC2.

Attachments (preview): control-plane-partition-v1.pdf (diagram), network-leakproof-flowchart_v2.png (flowchart), soc2-evidence-manifest.csv (manifest).

Questions for you to confirm so we can finalize the packet:
1) Is auditor interest limited to the four NimbusAI orgs we discussed, or do you want a generic packet that covers all Dedicated customers?
2) Any specific schema the auditor wants for traffic capture or pcap excerpts? We can provide sanitized flow logs if needed.

I’ve looped in Kimberly (security) and Priyom (infra) to own the evidence drop. Laura will coordinate the packaging and delivery.

Target: initial packet to you by EOD next Wednesday (2026-01-21). If that timeline is too aggressive, please advise.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: control-plane-partition-v1.pdf (diagram, 2 pages) | network-leakproof-flowchart_v2.png (PNG) | soc2-evidence-manifest.csv (CSV)
From: Alex Rivera <alex@nimbusai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control-plane partitioning and cross-tenant leakproofing — architecture snapshot and deliverables

Michael —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the attachments. A few clarifying requests from our audit lead before you invest more effort: 

- Scope: Please include a tenant-level egress flow for Dedicated (showing NAT/egress proxies, approved destination CIDRs) and an explicit statement about whether Private (on-prem) deployments can be configured to route control-plane calls through customer-managed KMS/HSMs.
- Control-plane surface: We need a list of control-plane endpoints (hostnames / generic path) and the auth methods used (mTLS, JWT + OIDC, or API key). We don't need production hostnames, just canonical endpoint names and whether they accept customer tokens.
- Evidence format: For SIG/SOC2 we prefer: 1) annotated diagram, 2) short narrative (<= 2 pages) mapping controls to CAIQ items, 3) one sample flow log for an admin API call (sanitized).

Also: does Redwood run any cross-tenant controllers that have write privileges to tenant-specific KV stores? If so, what guard rails limit that?

If you can respond to the bullets above and include the annotated diagrams, we can route them straight to our audit vendor (Olivia cc'd).

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of IT & Security, NimbusAI

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control-plane partitioning and cross-tenant leakproofing — architecture snapshot and deliverables

Alex / Olivia —

Thanks, good clarifying points. Short answers up front, with actions assigned below: 

1) Tenant-level egress flow: yes — for Dedicated deployments we run tenant-scoped egress proxies. I am attaching an updated flowchart (network-leakproof-flowchart_v2.png) that shows the egress proxy hop and approved egress surface. That diagram calls out how we apply destination allowlists and where VPC/NAT translation occurs.

2) KMS/HSM scope for Private: Private (on-prem) installs can optionally integrate with customer-managed KMS via our KMS proxy; we will include a table (kms-scope-table.xlsx) mapping keys used for model artifacts, control-plane tokens, and audit logs.

3) Control-plane endpoints & auth: canonical endpoints are documented in the attached PDF (control-plane-partition-v1.pdf). Auth modes: internal control-plane service-to-service uses mTLS + short-lived SPIFFE identities; external control-plane admin APIs accept OAuth2 bearer tokens (customer-scoped) and support OIDC federation. We will provide a short list of canonical paths (no production hostnames).

4) Cross-tenant controllers: Redwood does run global controllers (e.g., scheduler, autoscaler) that observe tenant metadata but write paths to tenant KV stores are mediated by an access control shim; writes require a per-tenant service principal and are audited. Priyom will include the runtime-level sequence diagram showing the authorization checks.

Action owners & timeline: 
- Priyom: runtime sequence diagram (authorization gates) + sample sanitized flow log for admin API call — ETA 2026-01-19.
- Kimberly: annotation mapping to CAIQ/SIG items (2-page narrative) — ETA 2026-01-20.
- Laura: package manifest and HubSpot upload (HUBSPOT-123456789) + deliver packet to Nimbus audit vendor — ETA 2026-01-21.

I’ve uploaded the in-progress artefacts to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CP-partitioning-docs (access granted to Nimbus audit addresses). Let us know if you want the sanitized flow log in a particular schema (CEF/JSON/etc.).

Regards,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Fwd: Control-plane partitioning and cross-tenant leakproofing — architecture snapshot and deliverables

Alex / Olivia —

Following up with a concise checklist for the SIG / SOC2 evidence packet so auditors have a clear expectations list. We will deliver the annotated packet by 2026-01-21 unless you request an earlier cut.

Evidence checklist (owner / artifact / notes):
- Annotated topology diagram (Michael / control-plane-partition-v1.pdf) — shows control vs data plane lanes, tenant overlays, and egress proxy hop.
- Tenant egress flow (Priyom / network-leakproof-flowchart_v2.png) — include policy enforcement points and sanitized sample flow log.
- KMS boundary table (Priyom / kms-scope-table.xlsx) — maps keys to artifact types and KMS ownership.
- Control-plane endpoint list & auth modes (Michael / short table in PDF) — canonical path + auth pattern.
- CAIQ mapping narrative (Kimberly / caiq-mapping-2pg.pdf) — maps packet items to SIG/CAIQ questions.
- Audit/ops evidence (Laura / soc2-evidence-manifest.csv) — sample audit trail entries, retention policy statement.

Delivery and access: we will upload each artifact to the Drive folder and share a single ZIP manifest for download. If Olivia's vendor needs verification that artifacts were generated by Redwood (hashes, timestamps), let us know and we will include signed manifests.

Open item for Nimbus: please confirm whether you want the sanitized sample flow log in JSON or CEF; we will default to JSON unless you instruct otherwise.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
